title: The Year of Savings Sal Khan Gave Himself to Make Maths Videos
conflicts: Savings period: eight months (Mountain View Voice) versus nine months (Khan to the Chronicle of Philanthropy and Diane Rehm); Khan's nine used. Doerr's first gift: Wired puts a small donation in 2009; Khan puts the $10,000 cheque nine months after quitting (about mid-2010); Khan followed. The $100,000: cheque texted 20 minutes after lunch (book excerpt in Fortune) versus wired that afternoon (Chronicle); the story says only that word came that it was on its way. Hedge fund named as Wohl Capital (Wired, Mountain View Voice) or Connective Capital elsewhere; not named. Audience: 'tens of thousands a day' in early 2009 (book) versus 'tens of thousands to nearly hundreds of thousands a month' (Chronicle); the book's wording used, attributed. Khan's February 2012 'less than $3 million invested' sits awkwardly with $1.5m (Gates) plus $2m (Google); not used.
notes: The checker's repeat screen flagged mary-okelo-makini-nursery-in-her-home-1978 as same-founder but let it through; it is a different founder and episode, so this looks like a false positive. Founder quotations are all from English-language interviews or his own book excerpt.
